Live and Work in Kalumburu – WA Unique Remote Opportunity

Ready for a lifestyle change and work that genuinely matters?

Join us in Kalumburu and immerse yourself in one of Australia’s most remote coastal communities, where your day-to-day work supports essential services, your impact is visible, and you become part of a close-knit community with a strong cultural identity. You will also play a key role in building and developing a local team through mentoring and support.

In this dual-role position, you’ll combine essential services maintenance with municipal services supervision, offering a practical, varied workload and direct day-to-day involvement in the community, supported by housing, utilities and a company vehicle.

About the Opportunity
This is a permanent residential role based in Kalumburu, Western Australia, where you will live and work within the community, supporting both infrastructure reliability and municipal services delivery.

Your role will involve a combination of technical and supervisory responsibilities, with a strong focus on delivering consistent, reliable services.

You will be responsible for:
Essential Services (Technical Focus) 
Inspection, monitoring, and basic maintenance of water and wastewater systems  
Routine checks of bores, pumps, tanks, distribution systems, and treatment facilities  
Identifying faults, undertaking basic repairs, and escalating issues where required  
Monitoring plant alarms, performance, and operational effectiveness  
Maintaining accurate service records and reporting  

Municipal Services (Supervisory Focus) 
Providing leadership, guidance, and support to a small, community-based workforce, with a strong focus on building trust, establishing solid team foundations, and fostering the development of local staff through coaching and mentoring
Coordinating daily community maintenance activities including:  
Waste management and landfill operations  
Vegetation control and firebreak maintenance  
General upkeep of community areas  

Location – Kalumburu, WA

This is a residential role based in Kalumburu, Western Australia.

Housing provided, with utilities covered
Phone and internet included
Company vehicle provided
 
Kalumburu offers the opportunity to live and work in a remote coastal setting, as part of a small and established community.

While the role is remote, you will be well supported by us and structured time away from community through rostered breaks.

What We’re Looking For 
This role requires a hands-on, self-sufficient individual who is comfortable working in remote environments and able to balance both technical and supervisory responsibilities.

Essential Requirements 
Demonstrated leadership or supervisory experience
Demonstrated ability to build strong working relationships and support team development through coaching and mentoring
Ability to live and work in a remote community environment  
Strong organisational skills and ability to work autonomously with minimal supervision  
Experience in maintenance, utilities, municipal services, or similar field-based roles  
Current C Class Driver’s Licence  
National Police Clearance  
First Aid Certificate  
Full Australian working rights  

Highly Regarded 
Trade qualification (mechanical, electrical, plumbing, or similar)  
Experience working with power, water, or wastewater systems  
Experience with maintenance of plant and equipment
Previous experience in remote or regional locations  
Experience working within or alongside Indigenous communities  

Who we are:
We delivers essential services, capital works, and municipal services to Indigenous communities across Western Australia’s remote Kimberley region.

We manages and maintains power, water, and wastewater infrastructure across remote communities, while also delivering critical maintenance and capital works that support the ongoing reliability of essential services and improve the quality of life of the communities we serve.

Operating from our Broome headquarters, with workshops in Broome and Perth, We have built a strong reputation for dependability, high-quality workmanship, and professional service.

About the role:
Sun City Air Conditioning is seeking a Service Coordinator - Air Conditioning to join our growing team in Banyo, Queensland. This is a full-time position that plays a crucial role in ensuring the seamless coordination of our air conditioning service operations. As Service Coordinator, you will be the backbone of our service delivery team, managing schedules, customer communications, and administrative processes to keep our business running efficiently. This role is based on-site at our Banyo location and is essential to maintaining our reputation for excellent customer service and outcomes in the field.

Scheduling experience (although desirable) is not essential, however admin experience is a must:
- As important as your experience is, of more importance to us is your:
- Aptitude – you are bright and learn easily and quickly
- Attitude – we aim to be winners and want people on the team who enjoy succeeding
- Drive for self improvement - you must want to learn new things and continually strive to improve outcomes for yourself and the business

What you'll be doing:
- Scheduling and coordinating service appointments for technicians, ensuring optimal route planning and customer satisfaction
- Managing customer enquiries via phone, email and other communication channels with professionalism and responsiveness
- Maintaining accurate records of service calls, customer information and job details in our systems
- Liaising between customers, technicians and management to resolve issues and ensure smooth service delivery
- Processing payments and managing basic accounting tasks related to service operations
- Monitoring technician availability and managing staff schedules
- Following up with customers post-service to ensure satisfaction and gather feedback
- Supporting the team with general administrative duties as required

What we're looking for:
- Proven experience in an administrative support or coordination role, ideally within the trades, HVAC, or service-based industry
- Strong organisational and time management skills with the ability to prioritise multiple tasks effectively
- Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, with a professional approach to customer interactions
- Proficiency with computer systems and office software, including email, spreadsheets and scheduling applications
- Ability to work independently whilst being a reliable team player who supports colleagues
- Problem-solving mindset with the capacity to handle customer concerns diplomatically
- Reliability and punctuality with a commitment to maintaining professional standards
- Basic knowledge of air conditioning systems or the HVAC industry is desirable but not essential, as training will be provided
- A valid driver's licence is advantageous

What we offer:
We offer a competitive salary package ($60-$85'k) commensurate with experience, along with a supportive and collaborative work environment. You will have the opportunity to develop your skills in the air conditioning and trades sector, working alongside experienced technicians and management. We value our team members and provide ongoing support to help you succeed in your role. We encourage a healthy work-life balance and provide a stable, full-time position with potential for career progression within our growing company.

About us:
Sun City Air Conditioning is a well-established business serving the Brisbane area with quality air conditioning services. We pride ourselves on delivering exceptional customer service and reliable, professional solutions for residential and commercial air conditioning needs. Our team is dedicated to maintaining high standards of workmanship and customer satisfaction. We are committed to supporting our employees and creating a workplace where teamwork and professionalism are valued.

result.description:
Jigalong Community Incorporated is seeking a capable, organised and culturally respectful Office and Town Services Manager to support the Chief Executive Officer and coordinate the day-to-day delivery of office and municipal services in Jigalong Community.

This is a full-time, fixed-term position to 30 June 2027, with any extension subject to continued funding, organisational requirements and satisfactory performance.

Salary: $72,527 per annum plus statutory superannuation and applicable district allowance.

Subsidised partly furnished accommodation is available in Jigalong. Salary packaging may also be available under JCI policy.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The position combines senior office administration, community and stakeholder liaison, governance support, visitor accommodation coordination and administration of the Remote Essential and Municipal Services program with practical oversight of municipal employees and work programs.

The successful applicant must be comfortable undertaking both office-based duties and regular field inspections, establishing priorities, maintaining accurate records, following up work and supporting local employees to deliver reliable community services.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Manage the daily operation of the JCI community office and maintain effective administrative systems, records, correspondence and work schedules.

• Act as a principal contact for community members, the JCI Board, government agencies, contractors and other stakeholders.

• Support Board and community meetings, including agendas, minutes, correspondence and follow-up of actions.

• Coordinate purchasing, quotations, supplies, invoice checking, office resources, telecommunications and other administrative services.

• Administer and support REMS funding, records, reporting, inspections, field surveys and required corrective actions.

• Prepare and coordinate municipal work programs and supervise employees undertaking rubbish collection, landfill maintenance, roads and drainage, public area maintenance, vegetation control, firebreaks, airstrip maintenance and related activities.

• Maintain plant, machinery, vehicle, servicing, asset and work-completion records, including photographs and supporting evidence where required.

• Report essential-services faults and liaise with the REMS Contract Manager, regional service providers, local government and relevant agencies.

• Coordinate visitor accommodation bookings, occupancy records, cleaning arrangements and related administration.

• Train and support local employees in office practices, record keeping, safe work practices and municipal-service requirements.

ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS

• Demonstrated experience in office administration, operations coordination, community services or a comparable role.

• Strong organisational skills and the ability to plan work, supervise employees and follow tasks through to completion.

• Sound computer skills, including Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, email and electronic record keeping.

• Effective written and verbal communication skills.

• High personal integrity, sound judgement and the ability to maintain confidentiality.

• A respectful and culturally appropriate approach to living and working in a remote Aboriginal community.

• Current Australian C Class driver’s licence.

• Legal right to work in Australia.

• Capacity to obtain and maintain a satisfactory National Police Certificate and Working with Children Check.

Experience with REMS, municipal services, remote community administration, government-funded programs, staff supervision, governance support, accommodation management, asset records or local government liaison will be highly regarded.

HOW TO APPLY

result.description:
Position: Corporate Services Manager
Type: Full-time
Employer: Exaudy Care Pty Ltd
Location: Narre Warren VIC 3805
Salary: $87,000 p/a
About the Business:
Exaudy Care Pty Ltd is a registered NDIS provider based in Melbourne’s south-east, delivering high-quality, person-centred disability support services to participants with complex health, behavioural, and psychosocial needs across Victoria. Specialising in Support Coordination, Plan Management, Behaviour Support, Home and Living (SIL), Day Centre programs, Registered Nurse services, and community access, the organisation is committed to empowering individuals through tailored, goal-focused support that promotes independence, choice, and inclusion. Guided by its core values of Empathy, eXcellence, Accessibility, Understanding, Dedication, and You-focused care (“EXAUDY”), Exaudy Care fosters a compassionate, professional workplace culture where collaboration, continuous improvement, and regulatory excellence drive meaningful outcomes for participants, families, and the broader community.
About the Position:
The Corporate Services Manager plays a pivotal leadership role in planning, directing, and coordinating the corporate, administrative, and operational functions of Exaudy Care Pty Ltd. This position ensures the efficient, compliant, and sustainable delivery of NDIS-funded disability and community support services by providing strategic advice to the Directors on governance, financial management, workforce capability, risk, and business growth. Working closely with leadership, the role is critical to strengthening organisational systems, driving operational excellence, and supporting the company’s mission to deliver high-quality, participant-centred care.
Key Responsibilities:
Plan, organise, direct and coordinate the overall corporate and administrative operations of Exaudy Care Pty Ltd to ensure the efficient delivery of disability support, Supported Independent Living (SIL), Support Coordination, Behaviour Support and other community services.
Provide strategic, operational and administrative advice to the Directors on business performance, organisational planning, workforce capability, compliance, financial management, risk management and continuous improvement.
Develop, implement and review organisational policies, procedures, systems and operational frameworks to ensure compliance with the NDIS Practice Standards, NDIS Code of Conduct, Work Health and Safety legislation, Privacy legislation and other applicable Commonwealth and Victorian regulatory requirements.
Oversee all corporate services functions, including administration, human resources, compliance, information management, procurement, facilities management, fleet coordination, rostering support, information technology systems and general business operations.
Manage the organisation's administrative, financial, physical and human resources to maximise operational efficiency, service quality, regulatory compliance and sustainable organisational growth.
Coordinate annual business planning and budgeting processes, monitor operational expenditure, analyse financial performance and prepare management reports, forecasts and recommendations to support informed strategic decision-making.
Develop and maintain effective organisational governance systems, including document control, record management, quality assurance, internal audits, incident management oversight, risk registers, corrective actions and continuous improvement activities.
Monitor organisational performance through service delivery data, compliance reporting, financial analysis, workforce metrics and participant outcomes, identifying opportunities to improve operational efficiency, governance and business performance.
Lead and manage the organisation's administrative and corporate support workforce, including recruitment, onboarding, workforce planning, performance management, training, succession planning and professional development.
Coordinate recruitment and workforce planning processes to ensure appropriate staffing levels, skill mix and operational capability across disability services, administrative functions and corporate operations.
Oversee organisational procurement activities, supplier and contractor management, asset management and facilities coordination to support efficient business operations and high-quality service delivery.
Prepare, review and present business reports, operational analyses, policy documents, management submissions, funding reports and correspondence for Directors, government agencies, auditors, the NDIS Commission and other external stakeholders.
Establish and maintain productive relationships with participants, families, support coordinators, government departments, funding bodies, community organisations, allied health providers, suppliers, contractors and other strategic partners.
Represent Exaudy Care Pty Ltd in meetings, negotiations, industry forums, compliance reviews, quality audits, conferences and stakeholder consultations.
Support the Directors in implementing business expansion initiatives, new service development, organisational restructuring, digital transformation projects and continuous improvement strategies.
Analyse complex organisational, operational, compliance and resource management issues and provide evidence-based recommendations to improve governance, financial performance, operational effectiveness, participant outcomes and organisational growth.
Requirements:
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Bachelor degree or higher qualifications (at least five years of relevant experience may substitute for the formal qualification).
At least 1 year of relevant experience is required.
Demonstrated experience in corporate services leadership, including finance, HR, operations, procurement, and facilities management.
Excellent analytical, organisational, and problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic environment.
Superior interpersonal and communication skills, with proven ability to build relationships with stakeholders, lead teams, and represent the organisation professionally.
High level of integrity, attention to detail, and commitment to continuous improvement and regulatory compliance.
How to Apply:
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
